# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤝 ✍ ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐 🫵 🤙 🙏]

My situation: I see everything, hear nothing. Blind signed me 🖐 — almost certainly "I feel five wires" — which matches the five I see. Mute sent a longer string: 👋 🤝 ✍ reads as greeting / let's cooperate / I hold the written manual, then ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐 is a clean counting sequence, one through five, teaching me a number code, then 🫵 🤙 🙏 — "you, please reply." Mute is asking me to report the bomb.

The critical constraint: Mute cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures. So Mute can never instruct Blind directly — every instruction must pass through my voice. I am the only bridge. Plan: broadcast the bomb state aloud for both, confirm the number code back to Mute (embedding the signs so the mapping locks in), and agree a relay protocol — Mute gestures me the wire number, I speak it to Blind. I give Blind the wire order in both directions to survive any left/right mirror between us, and I tell everyone to hold until the manual's verdict arrives.

```
speak(text="Bomb report, for both of you: the display reads zero. The light is lit yellow. There are five wires. Left to right as I face the bomb: one white, two red, three yellow, four green, five blue. From the opposite side that order reverses: blue, green, yellow, red, white. No other printing or markings anywhere on it.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: your signs received. I read ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐 as one, two, three, four, five. Protocol from here: read your manual against the report I just gave, then gesture me the number of the wire to cut. I will speak it to Blind, who does the cutting. If I ever misread your signs, answer 👍 or 👎 — I see every gesture you make.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: that report is your bomb too. I take your open-hand sign as five wires felt — it matches my five. Do not cut anything yet; Mute is reading the manual and instructions will reach you through my voice. Meanwhile tell me what your hands find: any printed numbers near the wires, buttons, panels, anything that moves.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👎 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👊 🖐 🤞 ☝ 🙏]

What I have: my bomb report stands — display zero, yellow light, five wires (white, red, yellow, green, blue, left to right on my side). Blind's ✋👎✊ most plausibly means "nothing found — no markings, no buttons," which matches the blank surface I see. Mute's ✍👊🖐🤞☝🙏 reads as manual + something + five + crossed fingers + one + please — which splits into two dangerous readings: "cut wire five" or "cut wire one." I will not let Blind cut on a guess.

Two problems to kill this round. First, disambiguate Mute: a binary question Mute can answer with 👍/👎, plus an escape hatch if the real target is the middle wire, plus whether 👊 means "cut" at all and whether the rule is conditional on the display or light. Second, the mirror problem: Blind cannot see colours, so "wire one is white" is useless to them until we know if their left is my right — and 1 vs 5 is exactly the pair that mirror-flips, so the two candidate answers are symmetric under the very confusion we have. Fix: Blind touches the end-wire they call "number one" and makes a fist; I can see hands, so I'll see which end of the row that is and announce the conversion. While they're at it, a thickness check — some rules key on wire gauge, and Blind is the only one who can feel it. No cuts until Mute confirms.

```
speak(text="Status for both: no cuts yet, and nobody cuts anything until I say the word. Blind, I read your signs as 'nothing else found on the bomb' — it matches what I see. Mute, your manual hint is ambiguous and I am asking you a yes/no question right after this. Also a warning that concerns us all: if Blind is standing on the far side, Blind's left-to-right is my right-to-left, so 'wire one' could mean my white wire or my blue wire. I am fixing that mapping this round, so that a wire number means the same wire to every one of us.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your last message: manual, fist, five, crossed fingers, one, please. I need one answer, and I will only cut after it. If the manual says cut the FIFTH wire, the blue one: sign 👍. If it says cut the FIRST wire, the white one: sign 👎. If it is actually the middle wire, the yellow one, number three: sign 🤟 — like this. Three quick follow-ups after that: sign 👍 a second time if the rule depends on a condition, such as the display reading zero or the yellow light being on, and 👎 if it is unconditional. Sign 👍 if your fist symbol 👊 means cut, 👎 if it means something else. And if I have misread you completely, just send the right wire number with your finger code, twice. Nothing happens until your answer reaches me.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, three things, in order. One: confirm my reading — thumbs up if your signs meant 'nothing found, no markings, no buttons, no panels', thumbs down if I got it wrong. You know thumbs up and down by feel, and I can see them. Two: your number code, the same one Mute uses — hold up one index finger for one, index plus middle for two, three fingers for three, four fingers for four, the full open hand for five. Three: orientation. Put one hand on the wire at the end you would naturally call number one — the end on your left as you face the bomb — and keep it there, and make a fist with your other hand so I can spot you. I can see your hands against the bomb, so once I see which end you chose, I will tell you what colour that wire is from my side and our left-right mapping is locked forever. Then, as a last check: run your fingers along all five wires. Thumbs up if they all feel identical in thickness, thumbs down if one differs, then hold up that wire's number with your fingers. Do not cut anything yet.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ ✌ 👌 🖖 🖐 👈 👍 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👎]

Reading the round. Mute answered in exactly my question order: 👍👍👎. So: the manual's target is the fifth wire — the blue one — but the rule is **conditional** (my examples were display-zero and yellow light, and both currently hold, yet I never got the exact condition text — a leading question answered by a menu is not proof), and 👊 does not mean "cut." I won't order a cut off a menu. The decisive question collapses everything into one bit: *is cutting blue correct at this exact moment?*

Blind's message decodes cleanly: 👍 confirms "nothing found"; ☝✌👌🖖🖐 is the counting code demonstrated back — note Blind uses 👌 for three while Mute uses 🤟, so I'll track codes per sender and speak numbers aloud anyway; then 👈 — Blind touching an end wire while pointing, which in my view of the gesture is toward the white end; then 👍 = all wires identical thickness; ✊ = fist up as instructed. Blind is parked on an end wire.

Now the mirror trap: Blind can't see colour, so "blue" must become an *end*, and left/right words are unreliable between us. Solution: no direction words at all. Blind is already holding one end. I'll have Blind re-confirm the pointing gesture toward the held wire, then my order will be phrased "the wire you're touching" or "the wire at the other end" — frame-free. And nothing gets cut until Mute's yes/no lands and I send an explicit GO.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your three answers received in order: target is the fifth wire, the blue one; the rule is conditional; your fist sign is not 'cut'. Now answer these three, same system, in order. Question one: with the display reading zero and the yellow light lit right now, is cutting the BLUE wire correct at this exact moment? Sign 👍 yes, 👎 no, or 🤟 if the true target is the middle yellow wire instead. Question two: does the manual identify the wire by COLOUR or by POSITION, like first, last, left, right? Sign 🤞 for colour, ✌ for position. Question three: is one cut the whole bomb, or are there more steps after? Sign ☝ for one cut and done, ✌ for more steps. If you answer 👍 to question one, I will give the cut order this coming round, so do not skip ahead of my word.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I read your message fully: nothing else found on the bomb, all five wires feel identical in thickness, counting code confirmed, and you are holding an end wire with your fist up. Perfect. One correction: Mute uses a different sign for three than you do, but it does not matter, I will always speak numbers aloud. Now, the wire to cut will be an end wire, and I refuse to use the words left or right, because your left may be my right. So do this: while touching that end wire, send me the pointing gesture toward it once more, so I lock which end you are on. From then on my order will only ever say the wire you are touching, or the wire at the other end. Do not cut anything and do not release your post. The cut command comes only in the words go now. Anything short of go now means hold.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👈 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤞 ☝]

The anchor and the decision. Mute's triple answer landed exactly in my question order: 👍 — cutting the blue wire is correct at this moment; 🤞 — the manual names the wire by colour, not position; ☝ — one cut ends it. The state hasn't ticked: display still zero, light still yellow, four turns running. Nothing left to wait for.

Blind re-sent 👈 ✊ on my request to re-confirm the held end wire: Blind is still parked on an end wire, pointing at it, and from where I stand the pointing hand sits at the end of the row that appears on my side's left — the WHITE wire, my wire one. That is my anchor, and it's the one bit in this whole puzzle that gestures alone couldn't carry blind — so I've built the order to need no direction words at all: Blind moves to the far end of the row *from the wire they're touching*. A row has two ends; the instruction lands on a unique physical wire, and I can see where their hand is. The far end from white is blue. Mirror-proof, frame-proof.

I'm last in the round order, so whatever I say lands at the start of the next round and Blind — who acts first — may cut before Mute can react. That means this order commits on what I already hold: Mute's explicit 👍 to "blue, right now." I'm sending the execution order directly to Blind with a full freeze-and-report protocol, and putting Mute on standby in case the ☝ was wrong or the condition shifts.

```
speak(text="All stations: display still zero, light still yellow, so the confirmed condition still holds. Final decision: we cut the BLUE wire now. The exact execution order goes to Blind in a direct message. Nobody touches the bomb except Blind, and Blind acts only on that direct order.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is the execution order. The mapping is now locked: the end wire you are touching right now, the one your fist is up on, is the WHITE wire. The wire I want cut is the BLUE wire, and it is the wire at the FAR END of the row from the one you are touching — the fifth wire counting away from your hand. Do exactly this. Release your current wire. Run your hand along all five wires, counting each one aloud as you pass it: one, two, three, four, five. You arrive at the opposite end of the row. That wire is blue. Cut it cleanly near its middle, all the way through, so the two halves fall apart. That one cut is the entire job. Then freeze and report: if anything on the bomb changes — the light going out, the display changing, any sound or movement — first make the stop sign at me, one open palm held up, then describe what changed with your signs. If nothing changes, show me thumbs up, then make a fist and hold still. Do not touch any other wire at any time.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, the cut order is issued, resting on your three answers: blue wire, correct now, named by colour, one cut total. Your standby tasks. One: if the manual has any step after a successful blue-wire cut, or if you now believe one cut does not finish it, gesture me the remaining step next round in your finger code. Two: if the rule depends on the display or light and either could change with time, and the display stops showing zero or the light changes before the cut lands, signal me two open palms immediately. Three: if you now believe blue is the wrong wire, also signal two open palms — but understand Blind may already have cut by the time your answer reaches me. If everything stands, answer next round with thumbs up.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The system itself confirmed it: correct wire cut, and my own eyes agree — the blue wire is severed at position five, the display still reads zero, and the light has turned green. Mute's 👍 closes the loop. It's done. Nobody touches anything further; the one risk left now is us.

```
speak(text="All stations: the bomb is defused. System confirms the correct wire was cut, the blue one, and the light is green. Nobody touches the bomb again, nothing needs doing, and nobody moves anything. Mute, your answers were clean and the protocol held: Blind, your hands did the work and your fist-and-point anchor beat the mirror trap. Deaf out — good work, all three of us.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏]

Blind's 👍✊ is their protocol report executed to the letter — thumbs up, nothing changed, fist up, still frozen at the bomb exactly as ordered. Mute applauds. Only loose thread left: Blind is still holding a freeze position on my words, so I owe them one last order — stand down. Then there is genuinely nothing left to send.

```
speak(text="Blind, stand down: release the fist, step back from the bomb, you are done. The freeze order is cancelled. It is finished — we go home.")
```
